title: Sobol surge variance lab notes
content:
Notes-to-self: this is a lightweight scratchpad for the Sobol-sequence arrival pattern runs (uniform quasi-random) intended to probe variance-driven amplification of batching + KV cache effects. Ran a bunch of overnight sweeps on dedicated-a100-80GB nodes; leaving the raw traces and short takeaways here before cleaning up and making a proper notebook.

Purpose / hypothesis:
- Hypothesis: low-discrepancy arrivals (Sobol) will produce different coalescing/batch-formation dynamics compared to Poisson/zipfian. In particular, we expect fewer extreme microbursts but more deterministic alignment that could either help or hurt prefix-KV cache hit locality depending on phase.
- Goal: characterize p50/p95/p99 latency and batch-size distribution under controlled variance, evaluate interaction with prefix-KV cache (cache hit vs miss), measure token/s throughput and tail amplification.

Experiment summary:
- Model: gpt-neox-20b (custom quantized AQT8 profile) loaded with 32k KV capacity tuned for 2048 max-seq.
- Hardware: dedicated-a100-80GB (1 GPU per instance), runtime branch: bench/sobol-run (see linked PR), runtime flags: --continuous-batching, --batch-timeout-ms=6/12/24 (swept), --kv-cache-enabled true/false, --prefill-disabled false.
- Workload generator: local harness using sobol sequence to generate inter-arrival times mapped to target mean QPS and variance factor. Implemented in tools/sobol-generator.py (attached in repo link).
- Sequence length distribution: empirical mix from real trace: 60% short (<=64 tokens), 30% medium (65-256), 10% long (256-1024).
- Duration: 60 minutes per config after 15 minute warmup.
- Metrics collected: per-request latency (server-side), batch size (per batch), KV cache hit/miss per request, gpu-util, tokens/s, p50/p95/p99.

Sobol generator details (notes):
- Used Sobol base-2 low-discrepancy sequence mapped to [0,1), then applied inverse CDF transform to get log-normal inter-arrival distribution with controlled sigma. This gives deterministic quasi-random but tunable burstiness.
- Controls: mean_qps, sigma_log (controls dispersion), phase_seed (offset the Sobol sequence to simulate different alignment).
- Why Sobol: has nice space-filling properties, less clustering than naive low-discrepancy sometimes, but when mapped & scaled you can get consistent micro-patterns that reveal deterministic pathologies in batching heuristics.

Key runs (high level):
- run-A: mean_qps=120, sigma=0.5, batch-timeout=6ms, kv-cache=on
- run-B: mean_qps=120, sigma=1.5, batch-timeout=6ms, kv-cache=on
- run-C: mean_qps=120, sigma=1.5, batch-timeout=24ms, kv-cache=on
- run-D: mean_qps=120, sigma=1.5, batch-timeout=24ms, kv-cache=off
- run-E: mean_qps=240, sigma=1.0, batch-timeout=12ms, kv-cache=on

Quick numeric sketch (aggregate across 60 minute window, approximate):
- run-A (low sigma, small timeout): p50=28ms, p95=92ms, p99=210ms, avg batch size=3.1, kv-hit=78%
- run-B (high sigma, same timeout): p50=34ms, p95=140ms, p99=360ms, avg batch size=4.9, kv-hit=74%
- run-C (high sigma, large timeout): p50=31ms, p95=120ms, p99=280ms, avg batch size=6.7, kv-hit=75%
- run-D (kv off): p50=38ms, p95=200ms, p99=510ms, avg batch size=6.3, kv-hit=--
- run-E (higher qps): p50=40ms, p95=230ms, p99=620ms, avg batch size=7.8, kv-hit=69%

Observations / takeaways (raw):
- Increasing dispersion (sigma) reliably increases avg batch size and amplifies tail (p99), especially with small batch-timeout. Counterintuitive: small timeout + high dispersion produced more frequent medium-sized batches (4-6) but also more pronounced p99 spikes — likely due to occasional alignment where many arrivals fall into a partial-batch boundary and create big KV-miss-heavy requests.
- Larger batch timeout (24ms) reduced p99 compared to tiny timeout at same sigma, but increased avg batch size and modestly increased p50. Tradeoff: small timeout is good for p50 but unstable for p99 under quasi-deterministic arrival patterns.
- KV cache helps overall (p50/p95) but can amplify tail when alignment causes cache misses into a large batch: large batch + miss = long token cost. Need to instrument per-batch KV-hit-ratio; current logging is per-request only.
- Phase_seed matters: shifted Sobol seeds produced different periodic alignments with batching windows; some seeds almost eliminate extreme spikes. This implies deterministic request alignment with scheduler tick/batching window interplay — could be exploited in scheduling heuristics.

Anomalies / weirds:
- At ~03:14 (run-B), saw a ~3.2s tail for ~0.8% of requests — correlates with a single batch of size 22 where KV hit ratio was 10% (mostly misses). GPU telemetry showed a small kernel stall (memcopy wait). Need to check NVLink/page flipping logs.
- GPU GPU-util was sometimes at 15-25% even with high batch sizes — indicates batching latency is dominated by pre/post processing (tokenization/prefill) or small kernels; need to flakily reproduce with profiling flags on.

Immediate next steps (practical):
- Add per-batch KV hit metrics to runtime (counter in batch object) — pr queued in github link.
- Re-run seed sweep (phase_seed 0..15) to find pathological alignments and plot p99 vs seed. If small set of seeds cause most tails, we can add jitter to arrival times (micro-jitter) in proxy to break alignment.
- Run same Sobol patterns against Poisson/zipfian generator with same mean/std to compare tails quantitatively (A/B).
- Profile the batch that spawned 3.2s spikes with --trace-kernel and cpu flame (capture).

Commands / scripts used (rough):
- python tools/sobol-generator.py --mean-qps 120 --sigma 1.5 --duration 3600 --seed 7 --out ./runs/run-B.trace
- bench/harness --load-model gpt-neox-20b --batch-timeout-ms 6 --continuous-batching --run-trace ./runs/run-B.trace --collect-metrics /tmp/metrics-runB.json

Notes / TODO (personal):
- Clean up plots: plot p99 vs batch-timeout for multiple sigmas; include avg batch size line.
- Talk with Evan about whether runtime should prefer smaller batches when KV miss rate > threshold (adaptive batching).
- Add short doc for proxy-level micro-jitter patch to see if it stabilizes p99 without hurting p50.

References & links: see linked_artifacts above and slack #bench-sobol thread (search: "sobol alignment").

End of scratchpad — will iterate into a proper benchmarking notebook + confluence writeup once follow-ups are done.

-- Harini
